transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Ruiz (CTO), Jordan Lee (Cloud Engineer), Priya Shah (Security), Evan Torres (PM)

Summary (auto): Discussed Private VPC deployment options for Summit Health, including VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 DR), egress IP control, KMS integration, and SOC2/audit requirements. Agreed to follow up with checklist and schedule deep technical session.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Alex, AE on the Redwood Private team, and Samira is our SE who'll cover the networking stuff.
[00:08] Maya (Customer - CTO): Thanks Alex. We are evaluating options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — but for PHI reasons we think Private VPC is the likely path.
[00:18] Alex: Totally, makes sense. Samira, do you wanna kick us off on the architecture options?
[00:22] Samira (SE): Sure. So Redwood Private can run in a customer VPC or via a VPC peering/transit setup depending on cloud. On AWS we support VPC peering and Transit Gateway, and we can expose a private endpoint via PrivateLink if you prefer no routing changes on your side. There are tradeoffs — latency, bandwidth, cross-account permissions.
[00:40] Jordan (Cloud Eng): Right, our main constraints are: primary region us-east-1, DR eu-west-1, and we have strict CIDR blocks that can't be changed. Also we route all outbound through a central NAT and have egress inspection. How do you handle egress IPs?
[00:54] Samira: Good question — for Redwood Dedicated/Private we can provide static egress IPs from our side if we host NAT in your account; alternatively if you peer to our managed infra, we can push traffic through customer NAT so egress IPs are controlled by you.
[01:10] Priya (Security): We need to ensure KMS integration for envelope encryption, and keys must be customer-managed. Also SOC2 and audit logs are a hard requirement. Can you integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[01:20] Alex: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for data at rest and HSM-backed keys for certain customers. We also emit audit logs to a configured S3 bucket or CloudWatch/Logging account — configurable retention. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[01:31] Evan (PM): Are there any region constraints for Redwood Private? We saw some docs saying certain GPUs are only in specific regions, and we need the inference to be low latency for our clinician-facing app in US East.
[01:44] Samira: We typically run in the region you prefer; our managed images and optimized kernels are in us-east-1 and us-west-2 by default. For eu-west-1 we can set up replication for DR but some newer instance types might be delayed. For latency SLOs we'd recommend keeping the service in us-east-1 for production.
[02:00] Jordan: For peering, do you require cross-account peering or can we set up a Transit Gateway attachment? We already use TGW for inter-VPC routing.
[02:09] Samira: Transit Gateway is supported and often preferred at scale. We can attach into your TGW; if you prefer peering, that works but you need to ensure no CIDR overlap and routing table entries are in place.
[02:21] Maya: CIDR overlap is a blocker for us — we have legacy ranges that collide with some vendor defaults.
[02:26] Alex: We can work around that by deploying in a dedicated account in your org and attaching via TGW, or use PrivateLink so you don't need overlapping route tables modified. PrivateLink gives you an interface endpoint in your subnet.
[02:38] Priya: With PrivateLink, do we still get audit logs and can we force TLS mutual auth?
[02:45] Samira: Audit logs are independent of the network transport — we still push logs to your logging account. Mutual TLS is supported on the control plane for certain configurations; data plane can be routed via PrivateLink and encrypted in transit.
[02:58] Jordan: What about IP allow-listing for our firewall? We need known outbound IPs from Redwood for firewall rules on our netops side.
[03:06] Samira: If we run components in customer VPC, egress is from your NAT. If we run managed infra and peer, we can provide a list of egress IPs or put an appliance in your account to NAT. We'll provide the egress IPs in the checklist.
[03:19] Evan: We also have a SAML SSO requirement and RBAC controls — who logs into the console, can we map to our IdP?
[03:27] Alex: Yes, SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning users is supported. RBAC maps to roles; we can sync groups from your IdP. We'll include details in the security docs.
[03:36] Maya: Any onboarding window or downtime to expect for cutover? Our clinicians need 99.9% availability.
[03:42] Samira: The private install can be done with canary routing and our rollout tooling — minimal disruption. Typical cutovers are planned with a canary and fallback to hosted if anything goes wrong. We'll recommend a pilot first, with limited traffic.
[03:56] Jordan: For pilot, what telemetry do you need from us? Are there specific sequence lengths, token distributions we should provide for benchmarking?
[04:03] Samira: Ideally a representative prompt set, typical context lengths, and concurrent user patterns. We'll run throughput and latency benchmarks with those to recommend instance types and batching profiles.
[04:15] Priya: On compliance, how long are logs retained by default? We may need 1 year for audits.
[04:21] Alex: Default is 90 days, but we can configure retention to meet your policy — we can export to your S3 for long-term retention and lifecycle management.
[04:29] Evan: What about data residency — some patient data must stay in-region (EU). How do you support regionally isolated deployments?
[04:36] Samira: We can pin workloads to regions. For EU data we would keep model hosting and any persistent storage in eu-west-1. For your use-case, if PHI must stay in-region, we'd deploy separate cluster in eu-west-1 for EU patients and us-east-1 for US, with routing at the application layer.
[04:50] Jordan: Is there support for Direct Connect / ExpressRoute? We have an existing Direct Connect to us-east-1 and would prefer private connectivity for bandwidth reasons.
[04:58] Samira: Yes, Direct Connect/ExpressRoute is compatible — you'd bring the private connectivity to your VPC and attach TGW or VPC peering. We can work with your network team to test throughput.
[05:10] Maya: Any blockers around our security posture? We use strict egress inspection and a managed WAF.
[05:17] Alex: Not usually; we adapt to customer perimeter controls. We'll need details on your egress inspection flows so we can ensure health checks and telemetry pass. Sometimes health checks are blocked by strict proxy rules — we have a checklist for that.
[05:30] Priya: Encryption at rest: is model cache encrypted? Who owns keys for cache?
[05:36] Samira: Cache and persistent storage can be encrypted with your customer-managed KMS keys. We support envelope encryption and can rotate keys per your policy.
[05:45] Jordan: Do you have any recommended subnet sizing or ENI limits we should be aware of? Our network team wants guidance to pre-allocate subnets.
[05:52] Samira: We'll provide recommended subnet sizes based on expected throughput. For GPU-backed nodes we typically use /24 subnets per node group to avoid ENI limits; exact numbers will come after we size the pilot.
[06:05] Evan: Can you share a sample network diagram or deployment template?
[06:09] Alex: Yes, I'll attach a reference architecture and a Terraform module we often use as a starting point.
[06:15] Maya: Timeline-wise, we want a pilot within 3 weeks if possible. Is that feasible?
[06:20] Samira: If we get the CIDR info and access to a test VPC, we can land a pilot in 2-3 weeks. We'll need a small team sync to align on security and network changes.
[06:29] Jordan: I'll share the CIDR ranges and existing TGW attachments after this call.
[06:33] Priya: I'll consolidate our compliance checklist and questions.
[06:36] Alex: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners — we'll list them in the follow-up email.
[06:42] Evan: One last question — cost model for Private: reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go?
[06:47] Alex: For Private we usually do a dedicated contract — reserved capacity for predictable throughput. There are options for burst capacity and a hybrid where you fall back to hosted for spikes. We'll include pricing options in the SOW.
[06:58] Maya: Awesome, thanks everyone.
[07:01] Alex: Thank you. We'll follow up with the checklist, security docs, and schedule the deep dive.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., TGW sometimes transcribed as T G W), occasional filler words. References to Redwood product names: Redwood Private, Dedicated, hosted API, and Optimize toolkit.
